# Save the drop for a song you already added

## What is wrong right now

When you add a song, the app checks whether it already has it. If it does, it skips
everything — which is right, and it is why re-adding a song costs you nothing.

But it skips **one step too many**. If you attach a beat you have already added, and the
app asks you where the drop hits, and you type it — **your answer is thrown away**. Nothing
on screen says so. The song keeps whatever drop it had before, which for your songs is
none at all.

## Why this is your problem specifically

Both of your own songs — _Heal the planet_ and _The drones keep droning_ — are stored as
**vocals, with no drop**. That is not an accident: until tonight, saying "this is a beat"
forced you to fill in a drop box, and saying "this is a vocal" did not. Calling everything
a vocal was the fastest way past a question the app should not have been asking.

So the moment you use the new `/grind my_beat:` on either of them and type the real drop,
you are standing exactly on this bug. **Without this change you cannot set a drop on your
own songs at all.**

## What the change does

One branch, in the file that accepts uploads. When the song is already here **and** you are
the person who uploaded it **and** you said it is a beat **and** you typed a valid time — it
saves the drop. That is all.

## What it deliberately does not do

- It does **not** change the song's name, its role, or who owns it.
- It does **not** let anybody else touch your song. Somebody else sending the very same file
  changes nothing at all — and that case is real, because a song is recognised by its sound,
  so two people can land on the same row.
- It does **not** spend any money or start any processing. Nothing about the paid path moves.

## If it is wrong

The worst case is that a drop gets written for a song where it should not have been. That
changes where the singing lands in future mixes of that song, and nothing else. It is not
permanent: adding the song again with the right time overwrites it. No audio is deleted, no
money is spent, nothing is exposed to anyone.

## Why I did not just do it

The upload file is on your "stop and ask" list, because it is the one part of the app that
accepts files from strangers. The rule is that I never change those while you are asleep, no
matter how small the change looks. So it is here, waiting for you.

## The safety checks

- The file still parses cleanly.
- Only the drop is written, and only for the row's own uploader.
- The free slot is released before this runs, so a duplicate still costs nothing.
- `library_store.upsert` merges rather than replaces, so no other field in the row moves.
- **Not yet run against the engine's test suite** — that happens when you approve it.
